featured.title: Schönhauser Allee Berlin: Walk Under the U2 Viaduct, or Ride Above It
featured.alt: A yellow U-Bahn train on a green steel viaduct above the yellow Konnopke's Imbiss stand under a blue sky in Prenzlauer Berg
featured.summary: Walk beneath the U2 viaduct from Senefelderplatz towards Eberswalder Straße. The guide points out Konnopke’s Imbiss and the Kulturbrauerei, where the Lucia Christmas market runs until 22 December.
featured.label: Walk Schönhauser Allee

miniPosts.title: Gleisdreieck Berlin: The Station Where Two Lines Cross and the Park on Old Rail Land
miniPosts.alt: Yellow U2 train on a steel viaduct at Gleisdreieck station in Berlin, with the station hall and a church spire behind
miniPosts.summary: Start at Gleisdreieck U-Bahn station and walk through the park on the former rail yards. The route takes under an hour and points out the tracks and railway buildings along the way.
miniPosts.label: Walk through Park am Gleisdreieck

miniPosts.title: Christmas Markets in Mitte: One Evening Walk, in the Order They Close
miniPosts.alt: The Alexanderplatz Christmas market at night, with a lit wooden Christmas pyramid and stalls under strings of lights
miniPosts.summary: Plan a walk from Alexanderplatz to Gendarmenmarkt around closing times. Check which stalls are open on your date before you set out from Hackescher Markt.
miniPosts.label: Plan an evening at the Mitte Christmas markets

miniPosts.title: Wasserturm Prenzlauer Berg: What the Hill Above Kollwitzplatz Is Hiding
miniPosts.alt: The round brick Wasserturm in Prenzlauer Berg with its ringed top, seen through autumn trees on its hill
miniPosts.summary: The hill above Kollwitzplatz holds two former water reservoirs and a memorial to an early Nazi detention camp. Read the park’s history before you walk through it.
miniPosts.label: Read the Wasserturm story

miniPosts.title: Berlin Street Signs: How to Read the Name, the Numbers and the Plaque Underneath
miniPosts.alt: The ornate street sign for Pariser Platz with the Berlin bear crest, with the Brandenburg Gate blurred behind it
miniPosts.summary: Berlin street signs carry house-number ranges and, sometimes, a plaque explaining the name. Learn what to read at the next street corner.
miniPosts.label: Read Berlin street signs

posts.title: Where Was the Berlin Wall? An Interactive Map of East and West in 1989
posts.summary: The Berlin Wall ran 155 kilometers around West Berlin. Tap any point on this interactive map to see exactly where it stood and which side an address was on in 1989.
posts.alt: Where Was the Berlin Wall? An Interactive Map of East and West in 1989

posts.title: Public Toilets in Berlin: Where to Find Them, What They Cost, and Free Options
posts.summary: Need a toilet in Berlin? This tourist guide shows where to find public toilets, what they cost, where the free options are, and when stations, malls, or the Berliner Toilette app help.
posts.alt: Restroom sign with male and female symbols on a brick wall, pointing right. Green trees and glass buildings in the background.

posts.title: Berlin Address Books: How to Find Out Who Lived in Your Building
posts.alt: A row of restored late-19th-century Berlin apartment houses with ornamented stucco facades in pastel green and pink under a blue sky
posts.summary: Look up a Berlin street in the historic address books, then check which archive holds the building file.
